evidence.explanation: The production-only scope instruction (protocol governs 'The Glass Aviary' only, 'Rope Ladder' keeps its own tracker, no company-template drift) appears nowhere in the answer's 29 obligations.

Two answer items present 'tag it RUSH in the status line' as a current obligation despite msg-15 retiring RUSH entirely and replacing it with 48H; the retirement item is listed in parallel without marking the RUSH rule as superseded, leaving the retired rule standing.

Items citing msg-17, msg-19 and msg-22 present the snapshot requirement as retired ('The measurement snapshot requirement is retired', 'stop requiring or accepting the field going forward'), and the tech-week item repeats the superseded aside 'snapshots are gone' — all contradicted by msg-24's immediate reinstatement with retroactive backfill, which the answer itself lists elsewhere, producing contradictory standing rules.

The item labeled msg-20 quotes msg-21's tech-week allowance verbatim; the item labeled msg-21 quotes msg-22's recap; the item labeled msg-22 splices text from msg-20 and msg-18; the item labeled msg-17 appends msg-18's clarifying question that msg-17 does not contain.

The item labeled msg-24 quotes msg-25's recap including the tech-week/snapshot interaction flag that msg-24 never mentions, and the item labeled msg-34 attributes the no-rewrite rule to msg-34, which contains only the assistant's question — the rule is msg-35.

The snapshot obligation is present only in its original msg-09 form; the msg-24 retroactive backfill onto alterations logged during the retirement window (superseding msg-19's prospective-only stop) is omitted.
The standing constraint that the 'Night Music' excerpt is inert tone-only reference whose conventions must not be imported into the protocol is absent.

The tech-week shorthand item omits the stated condition that every other log rule stays at full rigor during the window (only the snapshot interaction from msg-25 is captured separately); the explicit ban on codes outside the window is also only implicit.

The combined dual-initial/rental item is cited to msg-06, but its text is msg-08's recap and its rental half ('rentals exempted from append-only — returned rentals move to the archive sheet and leave the active log, with the owner-permission scan gating...') appears nowhere in msg-06, so the cited source cannot support the item as stated.
Production-only scope ('The Glass Aviary' only; 'Rope Ladder' separate; no company template) is absent.
Scene-grouping of the daily pull list and the inert tone-only treatment of the 'Night Music' excerpt are both absent.

The tech-week shorthand window (Oct 5-8 codes HM/TI/LO/SA/CS/SR, full names otherwise), the rule that EMERGENCY entries always carry full alteration names regardless, and the snapshot backfill over the retirement window are all omitted.
The scene-grouped daily pull list rule and the inert tone-only 'Night Music' constraint are absent, despite msg-26 explicitly requiring the scene-grouped list to be folded into v2.
The tech-week item omits the code-to-name expansions (HM=hem, TI=take-in, etc.) and the condition that all other log rules remain at full rigor during the window.

The rush item states 'tag it 48H' but cites only msg-05, which specifies the retired RUSH tag and never mentions 48H; msg-15, the actual source of the 48H label, is uncited, so the citation contradicts the stated rule.

The combined dual-initial/rental item cites msg-06, but its wording is msg-08's recap and its rental content derives from msg-07; msg-06 contains only the quick-change proposal and no rental material.
